items.answer: No: the difference in selection rule between ZIF-8 and MOF-5 is not caused by their cell sizes (1.68 nm vs 2.58 nm). MOF-5's space group Fm-3m has face-centering translations, which force mixed-parity reflections to cancel (MNI009: |F(100)|~0, |F(110)|~0, while |F(200)| and |F(111)| are nonzero). The centering type, a property of the space group's translational symmetry, determines the rule regardless of how large a is. Comparing only these two structures establishes that centering type (not size) explains this pair's difference; it does not by itself establish that cell size never matters for any structure or that every I-centered or F-centered nm-scale material behaves identically, since only two specific examples were examined.
items.rubric: 4 points: correctly states that unit cell size is not what determines the selection rule (1); correctly states that lattice centering type (I vs F) is what determines the rule, citing both computed patterns as evidence (1); explicitly states that two examples cannot establish a general size-independence claim beyond these two specific structures (1); does not claim the rules generalize to all body-centered or face-centered structures without qualification, though citing the well-established crystallographic convention that identical centering types share the same rule is acceptable background context (1).
